Brief facts of the case are that, the plaintiff - Panchajanya Vidyapeeta Welfare Trust (for short 'the Trust') being a registered trust filed the suit OS No.4249 of 2006 against defendant Nos.1 to 6 seeking permanent injunction restraining them, their agents etc., from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.

The schedule appended to plaint describes the property bearing No.28 (New Sy.No.28/1), measuring 5.10 acres situated at Malathahalli Village,
Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, with the boundaries mentioned therein.

sentences.text: It is contended that the plaintiff is a registered Charitable Trust and it runs several educational institutions.
The Trust is represented by the Managing Trustee.

Originally the founder Trustee - Sri M H Jayaprakash Narayan purchased the land measuring 2 acres in Sy.No.28 and 3.10 acres in the very same Sy.No.28 under two different registered sale deeds dated 31.03.1989, which is morefully described in the schedule appended to the plaint and referred to as the suit schedule property.

5. It is contended that pursuant to the Government Notification dated 11.11.1993, the Land Acquisition Officer notified the above said lands for acquisition for public purpose i.e., for running the Engineering College by plaintiff-Trust.

After completion of acquisition proceedings, the schedule property was handed over to the possession of the plaintiff and the name of the Trust was mutated in the revenue records as per MR.No.3 of 2000-2001.
The plaintiff paid the tax and is enjoying the property as absolute owner.
6. It is contended that the defendants tried to get the khata in respect of the suit schedule property without any right, title or interest.
They also tried to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment by the plaintiff by concocting the documents.
Since the defendants are politically influential persons, the plaintiff apprehends encroachment of the property by them.

The cause of action for the suit arose on 18.04.2006 when the defendants tried to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment by the plaintiff, attempted to demolish the compound wall and when the defendants tried to alienate the property.
Therefore, the plaintiff filed the suit seeking permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with its peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property.
7. Defendant Nos.1 to 3 have appeared before the Trial Court and filed the written statement denying the contention taken by the plaintiff.

It is contended that defendant Nos.1 to 3 are the lawful owners in possession of the property bearing Sy.No.28 measuring 2 acres situated at Malatahalli and therefore, the suit of the plaintiff for bare injunction is not maintainable.
It is further contended that the plaintiff has no manner of right, title or interest over the schedule property.
Only to grab the valuable property from defendant Nos.1 to 3, the suit is filed by the plaintiff.
8. Defendant Nos.1 to 3 contended that they have acquired right over 2 acres of land in Sy.No.28 by inheritance.

The property was originally belonging to one Surappa who purchased it under the registered sale deed dated 08.06.1951 and on his death, the property devolved on his only son Kenchappa, who is the husband of defendant No.1 and father of defendant No.2.
Thus, defendant Nos.1 to 3 are the absolute owners in possession of 2 acres of land mentioned above.

Defendant Nos.1 to 3 got changed the khata in the revenue records and thus the plaintiff is not having any right,
title or interest over the same.
9. Defendant Nos.1 to 3 pleaded ignorance regarding the establishment of the plaintiff-Trust and founder trustee purchasing 2 acres of land in Sy.No.28 under the registered sale deed.

They also pleaded ignorance about issuance of Notification for acquisition of land and the Tahsildar,
Bengaluru North taking over the possession of the property.
It is stated that since defendant Nos.1 to 3 are in possession and enjoyment of the property, taking over the possession by the Tahsildar or by the plaintiff-Trust does not arise.

It is contended that the plaintiff manipulated the records i.e.,

sentences.text: It is the plaintiff through its Trustees, which is making all efforts to grab the property.
Therefore, defendant Nos.1 to 3 prayed for dismissal of suit with cost.
10. Defendant Nos.4 to 6 have filed their written statement denying the contention taken by the plaintiff.

It is contended that even though the Notification dated 11.11.1993 for acquisition of land was issued by the Government of Karnataka, the said Notification was withdrawn as per Notification dated 18.01.1997.
The said Notification withdrawing from acquisition was challenged by the plaintiff before this Court.
But the withdrawal from the acquisition was upheld by this Court.
The said order dated 02.11.2001 reached finality and hence the plaintiff has no right over the schedule property.
The plaintiff is making all possible efforts to concoct the documents and to get favourable orders from the Court.
The plaintiff also concocted a document to show that the possession of the suit schedule property was delivered to a person in the year 1997 who in fact had died in the year 1995.
Sri S Mariswamy, the Chairperson of the plaintiff is a former Police Commissioner and using this influence, he is taking the law into his hand.
There are several criminal cases pending against the plaintiff and said Mariswamy.
It is also contended that the plaintiff is making efforts to encroach upon the property belonging to defendant Nos.4 to 6 with the help of anti social elements.
11. It is further contended that defendant Nos.4 to 6 are the absolute owners in possession and enjoyment of the schedule property.
The plaintiff is a stranger who is not having any right over the same.
The plaintiff concocted the documents and playing fraud on the Court.
When the Notification withdrawing proposed acquisition proceedings was issued, the plaintiff had challenged the same before this Court by filing the writ petition.

This Court had upheld withdrawal of the Notification,
vide order dated 11.06.1992.
It is stated that in all, there were 68 writ petitions filed either by the plaintiff itself or on its behalf by others.
All those writ petitions came to be dismissed during 2001.
Therefore, the plaintiff has no right over the schedule property.
In spite of that, the plaintiff filed the suit seeking various reliefs which is nothing but abuse of process of the Court.
If the contention the plaintiff is to be accepted, it is to be held that the person who died in the year 1995 had handed over the possession of the schedule property in the year 1997.
It is therefore contended that there is no merit in the contention taken by the plaintiff and prayed for dismissal of the suit.
12. Defendant Nos.4 to 6 have also re-iterated the contention taken by defendant Nos.1 to 3 regarding the influence wielded by Sri S Mariswamy, a retired Police Commissioner.
Under such circumstances, the plaintiff cannot succeed in the case.
Therefore, they pray for dismissal of the suit with cost.

"1. Whether the plaintiff proves that it is in lawful possession of the suit schedule property on the date of suit?
2.
Whether the plaintiff further proves that defendants are interfering with its possession of the suit schedule property?

The plaintiff examined PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to 28 in support of its contention.
The defendants examined DWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.D1 to D55.

The Trial Court after taking into consideration all these materials on record, answered issue Nos.1 to 3 in the Affirmative and accordingly, the suit of the plaintiff was decreed granting permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property.
15. Being aggrieved by the same, defendant Nos.1 to 3 and defendant Nos.4 to 6 have preferred separate appeals before this Court.

16. Heard Sri Sreevatsa, learned senior advocate for Sri S Sammith, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri H V Harish, learned counsel for Sri Rajesh Gowda, learned counsel for the respondents in RFA No.2272 of 2007.

Heard Sri Gowtham Dev C Ullal, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri Sreevatsa, learned senior advocate for Sri S Sammith, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 3 and Sri H V Harish, learned counsel for respondent No.4 in RFA No.2199 of 2007.
17.

Learned counsels for the appellants in both the appeals contended that defendant Nos.1 to 3 are the owners being the legal representatives of Kenchappa who purchased the property from its original owner.
M H Jayaprakash Narayan referred to in the plaint had purchased 5.10 acres of land under two different sale deeds.
A notification was issued by the Government proposing acquisition of the larger extent of the land including the schedule property for the purpose of plaintiff-Trust.
Subsequently, another Notification was issued de-notifying the land from acquisition.
When that de- notification was challenged before this Court by filing the writ petitions, the same came to be dismissed as per Ex.D54.
The Trust had challenged the order passed in the writ petitions by preferring writ appeals, but the writ appeals were also came to be dismissed.

Therefore, even if the contention of the plaintiffs regarding purchase of 5.10 acres of land by M H Jayaprakash Narayan is to be accepted, the same remained with the said M H Jayaprakash Narayan, but never vested with the plaintiff-Trust.
Exs.P7 and 8 are the sale deeds to substantiate the contention of the plaintiff that the property was initially purchased by M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
PW1 during his cross examination categorically stated that at the time of formation of the Trust, it was not owning any property situated at Malatahalli.
The possession of the property by the Trust is never proved.
There was no transfer of ownership by M H Jayaprakash Narayan in favour of plaintiff-Trust.
When the plaintiff has not placed any material to show transfer of ownership by M H Jayaprakash Narayan in its favour, it cannot seek any relief from the Court.

18. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the Trial Court restricted its discussion only regarding the issues framed i.e., regarding possession and interference, but it never gone into the fact as to when the property owned by M H Jayaprakash Narayan devolved on the plaintiff-Trust.
The Trial Court rejected all the documents and the contentions raised by the defendants without assigning valid reasons.

Even though the Trial Court referred to various documents in its judgment,

It has not claimed declaration of its title when the same is under serious dispute.
The Trial Court has not taken into consideration any of these facts.
Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court is erroneous and liable to set aside.
20. Learned counsel submitted that IA.1 of 2022 is filed seeking permission to produce additional documents.
The additional documents are the endorsement issued by Special Land Acquisition officer, Bengaluru and judgment passed in LAC No.92 of 1999, where the claim of the Trust was rejected.
These additional documents further substantiate the defence taken by the defendants and therefore, the application is to be allowed, in the interest of justice.
He further submitted that no opportunity was given to the appellants to have their say on such additional documents.
Further, in the proceedings before this Court, the appellants were not parties.
The property which is the subject matter of the writ petitions or writ appeals, cannot be identified.

Therefore, learned counsel for the defendants prays for allowing the appeals by setting aside the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court and to dismiss the suit of the plaintiff with costs.

21. 3.10 acres of land which was owned by Munihanumaiah and Ashwathappa i.e., father of defendant Nos.4 to 6 was sold in favour of M H Jayaprakash Narayan under Ex.P7, whereas 2 acres of land owned by husband of defendant Nos.1 and 3 was sold under Ex.P8.
The said 5.10 acres of land was acquired under the preliminary notification dated 11.06.1992 and the final notification was issued in respect of 5.10 acres of land on 11.11.1993.
The possession of the property was taken as per Ex.P10 dated 04.07.1997.
The award was passed as per Ex.P6 on 25.04.1996.
Ex.P1 makes it clear that possession of the property was taken for the benefit of the Trust.
On 12.09.1997, the possession was handed over in favour of the Trust.
The sale deeds or all these proceedings were never challenged by the defendants.

22. Learned counsel further submitted that during 2013, one Smt Huchamma challenged the preliminary and final Notification and also the award passed in respect of 5.10 acres alleging that she is the wife of M H Jayaprakash Narayan, by filing Writ Petition No.32714 of 2013.
The said writ petition came to be dismissed vide order dated 25.08.2021.
The petitioner in the writ petition had challenged the said order by preferring an appeal in WA No.1201 of 2021.
The said appeal came to be dismissed vide order dated 04.07.2022.

Learned counsel submitted that these are all the subsequent developments taken place before this Court and therefore, he has submitted the copies of such orders passed by this Court, which are all public documents.
23. Learned counsel also submitted that the Writ Petition No.18977 of 2012 was filed by the Trust against defendant No.2 and others which was disposed of 03.11.2015.

24. Learned counsel for the respondent contended that M H Jayaprakash Narayan was the Managing Trustee of the plaintiff-Trust and he was the settler as per - Ex.D15.
It was the Trust which paid the amount through M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
So the revenue documents stood in the name of M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
In the meantime, M H Jayaprakash Narayan died and the property was acquired for the purpose of the Trust.
Compensation was deposited in the Civil Court.
The proceedings under Sections 30 and 31(2) were held, wherein, there was rival claim between the Trust and legal representatives of M H Jayaprakash Narayan Jayaprakash.
The Special Land Acquisition officer has held that there is a bar for claiming the property benami by the Trust.
Trust could not have been the owner as well as the beneficiary.
So it was held that the legal representatives of M H Jayaprakash Narayan are entitled for compensation.
Even if the additional documents produced by the appellants are to be taken into consideration, that will support the case of the plaintiff.
The defendants have no manner of right, title or interest in the property and therefore, the Trial Court rightly decreed the suit of the plaintiff.

Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal with costs.
25.

In view of the rival contentions urged by learned counsel for both the parties, the points that would arise for my consideration is:
"1. Whether the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court suffers from perversity or illegality and calls for interference by this Court and whether both the appeals filed by the defendants deserves to be allowed?
2. Whether IA.1 of 2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC seeking production of additional documents deserves to be allowed?
What Order?"

My answer to the above points are in the 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 26.

It is the specific contention of the plaintiff that it is a registered Charitable Trust and 5.10 acres of land in Sy.No.28/1 of Malathahalli village was acquired for the benefit of Trust from Sri M H Jayaprakash Narayan who purchased this property under two different sale deeds dated 31.03.1989.
To prove this contention, the plaintiff produced Exs.P7 and P8, the copies of the registered sale deeds.
As per Ex.P7, one Kenchappa sold 3.10 acres of land in favour of M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
Kenchappa is none other than the husband of defendant No.1 and father of defendant Nos.2 and 3.

As per Ex.P8, 2 acres of land in Sy.No.28/1 situated at Malathahalli village was sold in favour of M H Jayaprakash Narayan by Munihanumaiah along with children Ashwathappa, Veera Mayappa and Shivanna.
Defendant Nos.4 and 5 are the sons of Ashwathappa and defendant No.6 is the son of Munihanumaiah referred to in the sale deed.
Both these documents are registered documents dated 31.03.1989.

are the encumbrance certificates, wherein the registered sale deeds dated 31.03.1989 executed in favour of M H Jayaprakash Narayan are referred to.

Thus, the registered sale deeds coupled with change of revenue entries on the basis of mutation and reference to the sale deeds in the encumbrance certificate supports the contention of the plaintiff regarding the ownership of 5.10 acres of land in Sy.No.28/1 of Malathahalli village by M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
27. It is the contention of defendant Nos.1 to 3 that they are the owners of 2 acres of land in Sy.No.28/1.
In support of the same, they have produced Exs.D1 and D2.
Ex.D1 is the certified copy of the sale deed dated 18.09.1951, under which the property was purchased by Surappa who is the father of Kenchappa.
Ex.D2 is the partition deed entered into between defendant Nos.1 to 3 on 09.11.2005 in respect of 2 acres of land.

It is pertinent to note that this partition was entered into between defendant Nos.1 to 3 much after the death of Kenchappa and after alienation of 3.10 acres of land by Kenchappa in favour of M H Jayaprakash Narayan under Ex.P7 dated 31.03.1989.

Defendant Nos.1 to 3 have not explained as to how they acquired right over 3.10 acres of land to partition it amongst themselves when their father Kenchappa sold the same in favour of M H Jayaprakash Narayan under the registered sale deed.

Any number of revenue records standing in the name of either Kenchappa or defendant Nos.1 to 3 will not support the contention unless the registered sale deed Ex.P7 is satisfactorily explained by them.

Kenchappa during his life time, never challenged the sale deed in favour of M H Jayaprakash Narayan, but on the other hand, the revenue entries were mutated in the name of the purchaser immediately after the sale deed.
28. Similarly, even though defendant Nos.4 to 6 claim title over 2 acres of land, the same was sold under Ex.P8 by Munihanumaiah and others in favour of M H Jayaprakash Narayan on 31.03.1989.
The said sale deed was never challenged either by the vendors or by defendant Nos.4 to 6.

There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the registered sale deed Exs.P7 and 8 with the revenue records corresponding to the sale deeds and the encumbrance certificates referring to the sale deeds.

Therefore, I do not find any reason to disbelieve the version of the plaintiff or to accept the contention of defendant Nos.1 to 6.
29.
It is the contention of the plaintiff that 5.10 acres of land owned by M H Jayaprakash Narayan was acquired by issuing the preliminary and final Notification for the benefit of the plaintiff-Trust.
To prove this contention, the plaintiff produced the Gazette Notification dated 11.08.1997 marked as Ex.P1 and Ex.P6 - the copy of the award passed in LAC No.8 of 1987-88.
Acquisition of the land by issuing preliminary Notification is not in dispute.

But it is the contention of the defendants that subsequently 5.10 acres of land owned by M H Jayaprakash Narayan was de-notified and thus the plaintiff-Trust had not acquired any title over the said lands.
The defendants have produced Ex.D25 the certified copy of the Notification dated 11.06.1992.
It shows the acquisition of 5.10 acres of land standing in the name of M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
As per Ex.D27 the certified copy of the Notification dated 14.04.1994, de-notifying several properties with different survey numbers.
It also includes Sy.No.28/1, but the area de-notified is 4 acres standing in the names of M H Jayaprakash Narayan and Putta Rudrappa.

sentences.text: Exs.D37 and 38 are the mutation register extracts in respect of 2 acres of land standing in the name of Kenchappa and Putta Rudrappa in respect of 4 acres of land.
As per Ex.D40, Putta Rudrappa was the owner of Sy.No.28 measuring 4 acres which was purchased by others.
It is also substantiated by the encumbrance certificate Ex.D41.

All these documents disclose that Putta Rudrappa was owning 4 acres of land in Sy.No.28, which he dealt with separately and it has nothing to do with the schedule property i.e., measuring 5.10 acres in Sy.No.28/1.
Ex.D44 is the RTC in respect of the land measuring 9.35 acres in Sy.No.28/1, out of which, plaintiff-Trust is possessing 5.10 acres of land and Putta Rudrappa possessing 4 acres of land.

Therefore, the contention of the defendants that 5.10 acres of land owned by M H Jayaprakash Narayan was de-notified cannot be accepted, but on the other hand, portion of land measuring 4 acres owned by Putta Rudrappa in Sy.No.28 was de-notified.
31. Ex.D54 is the certified copy of the order dated 11.08.2000 passed by the co-ordinate bench of this Court in Writ Petition No.4805 of 1997 with other connected writ petitions.
Writ Petition No.4805 of 1997 was filed by the plaintiff-Trust and others seeking to quash Annexure-E dated 18.01.1997 de-notifying the acquisition of 12.31 acres of land.
The said writ petitions came to be dismissed in the light of the subsequent developments and the writ petitions becoming infructuous.
32. Ex.D26 is the Notification dated 28.12.1992 notifying 4 acres of land in Sy.No.28/1 standing in the name of M H Jayaprakash Narayan and Putta Rudrappa.
Ex.D28 is the Notification dated 18.01.1997 de-notifying the said acquisition proposed under the Notification dated 28.12.1992.

If Ex.D28 is read along with Ex.D54, it is clear that the plaintiff-Trust had challenged the de-notification of 4 acres of land in Sy.No.28/1 as per Ex.D28, which is referred to in the writ petitions as per Annexure-E.

Therefore, the contention of the defendants that the entire extent of land which was acquired under the preliminary Notification for the benefit of plaintiff-Trust was de-notified and challenge to such de- notification was rejected by this Court, cannot be accepted.
33. From the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Court, the plaintiff is successful in proving its ownership and possession of the schedule property.

The defendants denying the right of the plaintiff and asserting their ownership right over the schedule property have posed threat to the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the same by the plaintiff.

Moreover, the plaintiff has pleaded and proved the interference by the defendants for seeking permanent injunction restraining them from interfering with its peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property.

34. The defendants even though asserted their ownership over the schedule property and contended that bare suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable, are not successful in probabalising the same.
On the other hand, the contention of the defendants claiming ownership over the schedule property is falsified by the materials that are placed by the plaintiff to seek ownership over the same.

The materials that are placed before the Court also substantiate the contention of the plaintiff that the schedule property measuring 5.10 acres of land in Sy.No.28/1 was acquired from the possession of M H Jayaprakash Narayan by issuing necessary Notification and subsequently the award was passed as per Ex.P6.

Even though an attempt was made to connect Ex.D54 the order passed in the writ petitions, to the contention of the defendants that the challenge to de- notification was dismissed by the Court and therefore, there is no acquisition of the land would fail, in view of the Smt Revamma vs Panchajanya Vidyapeeta Welfare Trust ... on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168901005/

36. The second document proposed to be produced is the certified copy of the endorsement dated 03.06.2013 issued by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Bengaluru, according to which, the Registrar of City Civil Court, Bengaluru, returned the voucher No.29/99-2000 dated 15.05.1999 for Rs.13,49,732/- in LAC No.92 of 1999 with objections raised by the Treasury, requesting for further action in the matter.
37. The third document proposed to be produced is the order sheet along with the judgment dated 08.06.2009 passed in LAC No.92 of 1999.

This proceeding was under Section 30 and 31(2) of Land Acquisition Act, whereunder, the plaintiff-Trust represented by its Chairman contended that he acquired the land measuring 5.10 acres in Sy.No.28/1 belonging to the first claimant Trust.

The reference Court after considering the materials placed before it, answered this point in the negative and held that second claimant was the legal heir of the deceased owner of the land who is entitled for compensation for acquisition of the land.

The reference Court rejected the claim of the plaintiff-Trust that the land in question was owned by the Trust even before acquisition since it was standing in the name of M H Jayaprakash Narayan and it is contended that said M H Jayaprakash Narayan was the founder trustee of the plaintiff-Trust.
On the other hand, the Court accepted the contention of the other claimants who claim the compensation for acquisition of the land being the legal representatives of M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
38. Even if these three documents referred to above are to be admitted in evidence, the case made out by the defendants will not improve in any manner.

On the other hand, the judgment in LAC No.92 of 1999 supports the contention of the plaintiff that the schedule property was in fact acquired and the compensation was ordered to be paid to the legal representatives of M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
It also falsifies the contention of the defendants that the schedule property was de-notified under any notification.

39. Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC bars production of additional evidence before the Appellate Court,
unless grounds specified under the Rule is made out.

When the documents are not relevant to be taken into consideration as they do not improve the case of the defendants in any manner, I am of the opinion that the appellants have not made out any ground to entertain IA.1 of 2022.
I am also of the opinion that the plaintiff-Trust is successful in proving the ownership and possession of the schedule property and the interference by the defendants.
Therefore, the plaintiff is entitled for the Smt Revamma vs Panchajanya Vidyapeeta Welfare Trust ...

It has taken into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before it and arrived at a right conclusion.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.

JUDGMENT Defendant Nos.1 to 3 have preferred RFA No.2272 of 2007 and defendant Nos.4 to 6 have preferred RFA No.2199 of 2007 impugning the judgment and decree dated 26.09.2007 passed in OS No.4249 of 2006 on the file of the learned XVII Additional City Civil Judge, Bengaluru City (CCH- 16), decreeing the suit of the plaintiff granting permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property by the plaintiff.
opennyai_summary.facts:
After completion of acquisition proceedings, the schedule property was handed over to the possession of the plaintiff and the name of the Trust was mutated in the revenue records as per MR.No.3 of 2000-2001.
The plaintiff paid the tax and is enjoying the property as absolute owner.
Therefore, the plaintiff filed the suit seeking permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with its peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property.
The Trial Court after taking into consideration all these materials on record, answered issue Nos.1 to 3 in the Affirmative and accordingly, the suit of the plaintiff was decreed granting permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property.
A notification was issued by the Government proposing acquisition of the larger extent of the land including the schedule property for the purpose of plaintiff-Trust.
There was no transfer of ownership by M H Jayaprakash Narayan in favour of plaintiff-Trust.
The Trial Court misled itself in holding that the plaintiff has proved possession of the schedule property.
The said 5.10 acres of land was acquired under the preliminary notification dated 11.06.1992 and the final notification was issued in respect of 5.10 acres of land on 11.11.1993.
The award was passed as per Ex.P6 on 25.04.1996.
Ex.P1 makes it clear that possession of the property was taken for the benefit of the Trust.
On 12.09.1997, the possession was handed over in favour of the Trust.
The sale deeds or all these proceedings were never challenged by the defendants.
Compensation was deposited in the Civil Court.
opennyai_summary.issue:
If the contention the plaintiff is to be accepted, it is to be held that the person who died in the year 1995 had handed over the possession of the schedule property in the year 1997.
13. On the basis of these pleadings, the Trial Court framed the following issues for consideration:
"1. Whether the plaintiff proves that it is in lawful possession of the suit schedule property on the date of suit?
2.
Whether the plaintiff further proves that defendants are interfering with its possession of the suit schedule property?
5 3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to the injunction as prayed for?
4. What Order or Decree?"
14.
In view of the rival contentions urged by learned counsel for both the parties, the points that would arise for my consideration is:
"1. Whether the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court suffers from perversity or illegality and calls for interference by this Court and whether both the appeals filed by the defendants deserves to be allowed?
2. Whether IA.1 of 2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC seeking production of additional documents deserves to be allowed?
What Order?"
My answer to the above points are in the 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 26.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
When the plaintiff has not placed any material to show transfer of ownership by M H Jayaprakash Narayan in its favour, it cannot seek any relief from the Court.
19. Learned counsel submitted that when the plaintiff has not proved its possession over the schedule property, it cannot succeed in a suit for permanent injunction.
It has not claimed declaration of its title when the same is under serious dispute.
So the revenue documents stood in the name of M H Jayaprakash Narayan.
The Special Land Acquisition officer has held that there is a bar for claiming the property benami by the Trust.
Trust could not have been the owner as well as the beneficiary.
So it was held that the legal representatives of M H Jayaprakash Narayan are entitled for compensation.
The defendants have no manner of right, title or interest in the property and therefore, the Trial Court rightly decreed the suit of the plaintiff.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Trial Court has not taken into consideration any of these facts.
Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court is erroneous and liable to set aside.
The said sale deed was never challenged either by the vendors or by defendant Nos.4 to 6.
It is the contention of the plaintiff that 5.10 acres of land owned by M H Jayaprakash Narayan was acquired by issuing the preliminary and final Notification for the benefit of the plaintiff-Trust.
33. From the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Court, the plaintiff is successful in proving its ownership and possession of the schedule property.
The defendants denying the right of the plaintiff and asserting their ownership right over the schedule property have posed threat to the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the same by the plaintiff.
Moreover, the plaintiff has pleaded and proved the interference by the defendants for seeking permanent injunction restraining them from interfering with its peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property.
34. The defendants even though asserted their ownership over the schedule property and contended that bare suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable, are not successful in probabalising the same.
35. The appellants in RFA No.2272 of 2007 have filed an application under XLI Rule 27 of CPC seeking permission to produce additional documents to substantiate their contention.
This proceeding was under Section 30 and 31(2) of Land Acquisition Act, whereunder, the plaintiff-Trust represented by its Chairman contended that he acquired the land measuring 5.10 acres in Sy.No.28/1 belonging to the first claimant Trust.
The reference Court after considering the materials placed before it, answered this point in the negative and held that second claimant was the legal heir of the deceased owner of the land who is entitled for compensation for acquisition of the land.
The reference Court rejected the claim of the plaintiff-Trust that the land in question was owned by the Trust even before acquisition since it was standing in the name of M H Jayaprakash Narayan and it is contended that said M H Jayaprakash Narayan was the founder trustee of the plaintiff-Trust.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The said writ petition came to be dismissed vide order dated 25.08.2021.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.
Hence I answer the above points in the Negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) IA.1 of 2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC seeking to produce additional documents is dismissed.
( ii )
Both the appeals are dismissed with costs.
